question: On 20 new small synthetic binary prediction tables, do the implemented event tests agree with exhaustive correction enumeration, and how do the exact edge relaxation and separate-event bound compare with the exact first violating budget?
status: Exploratory implementation check; not a practical-benefit study.
weights: Uniform over all 15 reference-ordered model pairs
tie_rule: Recorded accuracy ties use model index. Only strict corrected-score reversals count.
generator: NumPy default_rng separately initialized for each listed seed. Binary true labels; normal difficulty with mean 0 and standard deviation 1.5; normal model skill with mean 2 and standard deviation 0.15; logistic correctness; independent 0.03 recorded-label flips. Flag the 12 largest model-disagreement counts, with example-index ties.
exact_reference: Enumerate all 4096 correction subsets per instance; flip recorded labels and recompute model counts independently of gain formulas. Check all 13 budgets.
graph_method: Exact maximum matching and vertex cover in the bipartite double cover. Export half-integral primal and dual certificates. Verify integer inequalities and equal objectives. Normalize by 15.
attempts: One attempt per listed instance. No replacements, parameter changes, enlargement, or rerun after seeing outcomes. Unattempted, incomplete, failed, and complete records remain distinct.
validation: One independent saved-input verification pass checks all correction subsets and exact certificates.
reporting: Report every planned instance and each status. Report finite breakdown and no-violation counts separately. Preserve each budget result and certificate. No conditional ratio using r+1 as a finite breakdown. No speed or real-world benefit claim. A failed mandatory check blocks manuscript inclusion.
